quote.quote: The telaprevir NDA was presented to the Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee on April 28, 2011.

An Advisory Committee meeting was convened on April 28, 2011 to discuss the merits of this NDA and the risk/benefit assessment for telaprevir in combination with Peg-IFN/ribavirin as treatment for chronic HCV infection.

recommendation.text: The committee voted unanimously to recommend approval: 18 Yes, 0 No, 0 Abstain.

quote.quote: On the question of whether telaprevir should be approved the Committee voted Yes 18; No 0; and Abstain 0.

linkages.concern: The committee was concerned that Blacks/African Americans and patients with cirrhosis were under-represented in the trials, leaving the optimal regimen/duration in these subgroups uncertain, and recommended additional study.
linkages.change: Postmarketing requirements/commitments include clinical trials to further evaluate response in patients with cirrhosis and in Black/African American patients.

concern_quote.quote: The Committee recommended additional studies in Black/African American patients and patients with cirrhosis at baseline.

change_quote.quote: clinical trials to further evaluate response in patients with cirrhosis and Blacks/African American patients

linkages.concern: The committee raised the serious-skin-reaction risk and suggested, among other mitigations, potentially maintaining a registry of patients who develop rash to identify predictors of serious skin reactions.
linkages.change: Postmarketing requirements/commitments include additional work to evaluate genomic factors that might be risk factors for skin adverse events.

concern_quote.quote: even potentially having a registry of patients who develop rash to try to identify predictors of serious skin reactions

change_quote.quote: additional work to further evaluate for genomic factors that might be identified as risk factors for skin adverse events

linkages.concern: The committee found the evidence less strong for response-guided therapy (RGT) in prior relapsers and did not reach consensus on its adequacy, but was permissive of the approach.
linkages.change: The approval adopted a response-guided therapy approach not only for treatment-naive patients but also for patients who had relapsed after prior Peg-IFN/ribavirin therapy.

concern_quote.quote: Although the Committee did not reach consensus on the adequacy of data to support approval of RGT in prior relapsers, they appeared to be permissive of this approach.

change_quote.quote: I also recommend approval of a response-guided therapy approach to the treatment of patients who have not received previous treatment and for those who have relapsed after prior treatment with a Peg-IFN/ribavirin regimen.

summary: The telaprevir (INCIVEK) NDA was reviewed by the Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee on April 28, 2011, which voted unanimously (18 Yes, 0 No, 0 Abstain) that the benefits outweighed the risks of rash and anemia and supported approval. The committee's concerns about under-representation of cirrhotic and Black/African American patients, and about serious skin reactions, map onto postmarketing requirements/commitments for subgroup trials and for evaluating genomic risk factors for skin adverse events. The committee was permissive of response-guided therapy in prior relapsers despite weaker data, consistent with the approval adopting RGT for both naive and prior-relapser patients; no formal REMS was required, with a Medication Guide used instead.
